title: International Evidence-based Guideline for the Assessment and Management of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
organisation: Monash University, ESHRE, ASRM and partners
summary: Healthy eating and regular physical activity are recommended as first-line support for the metabolic and reproductive features of PCOS. No single diet has been shown to be superior; sustainable patterns matter more than specific rules.

title: Testing and interpreting measures of ovarian reserve: a committee opinion
organisation: American Society for Reproductive Medicine, Practice Committee
summary: AMH and antral follicle count reflect the quantity of remaining eggs, not their quality, and are weak predictors of natural conception in the general population. Results must be interpreted by a clinician in context.

title: WHO laboratory manual for the examination and processing of human semen, 6th edition
summary: Provides reference distributions for semen parameters (for example concentration, motility, volume). A value below a reference limit is not by itself a diagnosis; results vary between samples and need clinical interpretation.

title: Smoking and infertility: a committee opinion
organisation: American Society for Reproductive Medicine, Practice Committee
summary: Smoking is associated with reduced fertility in women, earlier menopause and changes in semen parameters in men. Several effects appear to improve after stopping.

title: Obesity and reproduction: a committee opinion
organisation: American Society for Reproductive Medicine, Practice Committee
summary: Higher body weight is associated with ovulation changes in women and semen parameter changes in men. Modest, sustained changes in weight and activity can be associated with improved ovulation.

title: Female age-related fertility decline (Committee Opinion 589)
organisation: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists
summary: Fertility gradually declines from the early thirties and more noticeably from the mid-thirties. Age is the strongest non-modifiable factor, but it describes a population trend, not an individual's outcome.

title: Fertility problems: assessment and treatment (CG156)
organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
summary: Offers lifestyle guidance and describes when an assessment is appropriate, including earlier review for people aged 36 or over or with a known reason to seek advice.

title: Preconception care: maximizing the gains for maternal and child health
summary: Preconception counselling and care can improve health before pregnancy and outcomes for parents and children.

title: Sleep, sleep disturbance, and fertility in women
summary: Sleep disturbance and shift work are associated with menstrual irregularity and may influence reproductive hormones. Causation is not established.

title: Preconception stress increases the risk of infertility: results from a couple-based prospective cohort study
organisation: Human Reproduction (Lynch et al., LIFE study)
summary: Higher stress biomarkers were associated with longer time to pregnancy in one prospective cohort. Stress does not by itself cause infertility, and most people under stress conceive.

title: The therapeutic value of laughter in medicine
organisation: Alternative Therapies in Health and Medicine (Mora-Ripoll)
summary: Laughter is associated with lower stress hormones and improved mood in small studies. There is no direct evidence that laughter changes conception; it is included as a wellbeing and stress-buffering factor.

title: Social relationships and mortality risk: a meta-analytic review
summary: Strong social relationships are consistently associated with better health and wellbeing. Included here as a general wellbeing factor, not as a fertility claim.

title: Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of thyroid disease during pregnancy and the postpartum
summary: Thyroid dysfunction is associated with menstrual irregularity and pregnancy outcomes. Testing is a clinical decision based on symptoms and history.

title: Seminal and molecular evidence that sauna exposure affects human spermatogenesis
summary: Repeated scrotal heat exposure is associated with temporary changes in semen parameters that recover after exposure stops.

title: Semen quality and alcohol intake: a systematic review and meta-analysis
summary: Regular alcohol intake is associated with lower semen volume and altered morphology; occasional intake showed little effect.

title: Antioxidants for male subfertility (Cochrane Review)
organisation: Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews (de Ligny et al.)
summary: Evidence that antioxidant supplements improve live birth is of low certainty. A varied diet rich in fruit, vegetables and whole grains is reasonable general advice; supplements are a clinician conversation.

title: Planned oocyte cryopreservation for women seeking to preserve future reproductive potential
organisation: American Society for Reproductive Medicine, Ethics Committee
summary: Describes what a fertility-preservation discussion involves, including realistic expectations and limits. It is a conversation with a specialist, not a recommendation this tool can make.

title: Screening for perinatal depression (Committee Opinion 757)
organisation: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists
summary: Mood and anxiety symptoms during and after pregnancy are common and treatable. Screening and timely support are recommended.

title: WHO guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour
summary: Adults are advised to do at least 150 to 300 minutes of moderate activity per week for general health. This is general health guidance, not a fertility prescription.
